candidate_concepts.label: Minimax Regret Decision Criterion
candidate_concepts.description: A decision rule selects actions to minimize the maximum regret over all possible payoff distributions, where regret is the difference between the best achievable payoff and the payoff obtained.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain what minimax regret means.
Student can identify a decision scenario where such a criterion would apply.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The paper defines minimax regret as minimizing the maximum regret over all decision problems and centers its investigation on this criterion.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept is a foundational decision-making criterion that can be assessed with a single definition and a simple example.

candidate_concepts.source_name: How to Minimize Maximum Regret in Repeated Decision Making

candidate_concepts.label: Regret Definition and Calculation
candidate_concepts.description: Regret is the discounted sum of differences between the maximum expected payoff and the actual expected payoff per round, measuring loss due to ignorance of the optimal action.
coverage_criteria: Student can state the formula for regret.
Student can compute regret for a simple decision problem with given payoffs and a specified rule.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The paper explicitly defines regret in Section 2 as the discounted value of opportunity loss and uses it throughout the analysis.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: The definition is precise and can be checked by asking the student to write the regret formula and apply it.

candidate_concepts.label: Bernoulli Equivalent Decision Rule
candidate_concepts.description: A rule that can be applied to any payoff environment by behaving as if in a Bernoulli environment where success probabilities equal expected payoffs, using randomization based on observed payoffs.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain how a Bernoulli equivalent rule transforms continuous payoffs into binary outcomes.
Student can give an example of applying such a rule.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The paper introduces Bernoulli equivalent rules in Section 3.2 and proves they are essential for extending minimax regret results to continuous payoffs.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept is a specific technique that can be tested by having the student describe the transformation procedure.

candidate_concepts.source_name: How to Minimize Maximum Regret in Repeated Decision Making

candidate_concepts.label: Worst Case Prior in Decision Making
candidate_concepts.description: The prior distribution over decision problems that maximizes the expected regret of a Bayesian optimal rule. Minimax regret rules are Bayesian optimal under such a prior.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain its role in characterizing minimax regret behavior.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The paper defines worst case prior in Section 3.3 and proves that minimax regret is attained iff the rule is Bayesian optimal under a worst case prior.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: The concept is discrete and can be checked by asking the student to recall the definition and its connection to minimax regret.

candidate_concepts.source_name: How to Minimize Maximum Regret in Repeated Decision Making

candidate_concepts.label: Single Round Memory Rule for Two-Armed Bandit
candidate_concepts.description: A rule with only one round of memory that attains minimax regret when the discount factor δ ≤ √2 − 1 ≈ 0.41. It chooses each action equally initially, then repeats the previous action with probability equal to the payoff received.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe the rule's behavior.
Student can state the discount factor range where it is optimal.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Section 4.2.1 explicitly derives this rule and proves it attains minimax regret for δ ≤ 0.41.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: The rule is simple and can be tested by asking the student to implement it for a given sequence of payoffs.

candidate_concepts.source_name: How to Minimize Maximum Regret in Repeated Decision Making

candidate_concepts.label: Two-Round Memory Rule (Robbins' Rule)
candidate_concepts.description: A rule with two rounds of memory that attains minimax regret for δ ≤ (√5 − 1)/2 ≈ 0.62. For binary payoffs, it prescribes staying after a success and switching only after two consecutive failures; for continuous payoffs, a linear extension is used.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the rule's behavior for binary payoffs.
Student can identify the discount factor bound where it is optimal.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Section 4.2.2 presents the two-round memory rule and proves its optimality for δ ≤ 0.62.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: The rule's description in terms of a stochastic automaton is checkable with a few state transitions.

candidate_concepts.label: Minimax Regret and Bayesian Optimality Equivalence
candidate_concepts.description: Any rule that attains minimax regret is Bayesian optimal under a worst case prior, establishing a formal connection between distribution-free and Bayesian decision theories.
coverage_criteria: Student can state the theorem linking minimax regret to Bayesian optimality.
Student can sketch the proof idea (minimax theorem / zero-sum game).

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Proposition 1 in Section 3.3 states this equivalence, and the paper discusses it extensively.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a key theoretical link that can be tested by asking the student to explain the relationship.

candidate_concepts.label: Continuous Payoff Model (S-Model) in Bandit Problems
candidate_concepts.description: The extension of two-armed bandit problems from binary payoffs (Bernoulli model) to continuous payoffs in [0,1] (S-model), handled via Bernoulli equivalent rules that maintain linearity.
coverage_criteria: Student can differentiate between the Bernoulli model and the S-model.
Student can explain why Bernoulli equivalent rules are needed for the S-model.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The paper introduces the S-model (payoffs in [0,1]) in Section 2 and demonstrates how Bernoulli equivalent rules extend results from binary payoffs.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: The distinction is clear and can be tested by asking the student to provide examples of each model.

source_local_connector_candidates.reason: The paper proves that a rule attains minimax regret if and only if it is Bayesian optimal under a worst case prior (Proposition 1), connecting the minimax criterion directly to the concept of worst case prior.

The characterization of minimax regret relies on Bernoulli equivalent rules; Proposition 1 shows that a minimax regret rule can be found within the set of Bernoulli equivalent symmetric rules, linking the technique to the criterion.

The single round memory rule is optimal for lower discount factors (δ ≤ 0.41), while the two-round memory rule extends the range of optimality to higher discount factors (δ ≤ 0.62), showing a progression in needed memory complexity.
